text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Israeli soldiers kill 60-year-old Palestinian north of Jerusalem, tension ahead of government decision on Har Homa project to build more Jewish homes in East Jerusalem.
- Police and prosecutors believe Prime Minister Netanyahu should be questioned again in corruption affair.
- Industrial production grew by only 5.5 percent in 1996.
- Foreign investment in Israeli stock market rose to 1.9 billion shekels in 1996.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Tension in the West Bank and Gaza, Palestinian killed, Har Homa project to be approved today.
- Police seize documents from office of former attorney general Roni Bar-On in investigation of alleged government corruption.
- Palestinian Authority decides on non-violent response to Har Homa at this stage.
- Tel Aviv stock market drops 6.5 percent in five days of trading.
- U.S. insurance company AIG to begin operating in Israel in May.
- Israeli-Canadian tax treaty to be revised soon.
- Australia-New Zealand Bank to open branch in East Jerusalem next week.
MAARIV
- Israeli security forces to react with full force if Palestinians respond with violence to Har Homa decision.
- Saudi pressure torpedos Israeli participation in water fair in Oman.
GLOBES
- Industrial production rose only 5.5 percent in 1996, slowest increase in the last six years.
- Tel Aviv stock exchange is nervous over political crisis stemming from police investigation of alleged government corruption.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli army kills one in Hizmeh clash in West Bank.
- Har Homa approval today, Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan puts off visit.
- Disgrunted settlers forming new group.
